html:
The New Zealand Wars were fought from 1845 to 1872 between the colonial government, with British troops, and many Māori groups, mostly in the North Island. Land was at the heart of them.

After the Treaty of Waitangi, settlers pressed for more land. The largest war was the invasion of the Waikato in 1863, aimed at the King movement. Māori built clever earthwork forts, the pā.

Afterwards the government confiscated huge areas. Peaceful resistance followed, as at Parihaka in 1881. The confiscations are a main subject of claims before the Waitangi Tribunal. See Musket Wars.
